# Multi-Modal Dysgraphia Detection from Static Handwriting

[![Python 3.10+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10+-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)
[![Research: Verified](https://img.shields.io/badge/Validation-Tablet%20Sensors-green.svg)](report.md)

This repository provides an automated, clinically grounded **17-dimensional multimodal feature extraction engine** for screening dysgraphia directly from static 2D handwriting photographs or scans. The system unites standardized clinical spatial indicators (**Branch A: 9 BHK Diagnostic Features**) and neuromotor fluency estimators (**Branch B: Kinematic Trajectory Recovery & Multi-Level Ground-Truth Validation**) into a single, high-performance Python package.

## 3. Scientific Models, Clinical Frameworks & Technology Stack

### 3.1 Biophysical & Mathematical Models (The Physics Engine)

| Model | What It Does | Why It Was Used |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Two-Thirds Power Law**<br>($v(t) = \alpha \cdot \kappa(t)^{-1/3}$) | Relates hand velocity $v(t)$ to trajectory curvature $\kappa(t)$. | A fundamental law of human neuromuscular motor control (Lacquaniti et al., 1983). It allows us to estimate physical writing speed from a static centerline—the hand slows down on sharp curves and accelerates along straight lines. |
| **Boundary Minimum-Jerk Envelope**<br>($\sin^{1/2}(\pi s / L)$) | Shapes the velocity profile of each stroke to start at $0$ (touchdown) and end at $0$ (liftoff). | Mimics the physiological acceleration and deceleration constraints of human finger/wrist motor programs. |
| **Scale-Invariant NVI Model**<br>($\text{NVI} / \text{stroke}$) | Counts the Number of Velocity Inversions (peaks + troughs) normalized per physical stroke. | Quantifies motor hesitation, dysfluency, and neuromotor tremor independently of image size or camera zoom. |
| **Shannon Information Entropy**<br>($H = -\sum p_k \log_2 p_k$) | Measures the disorder/irregularity of normalized horizontal gaps between letters. | Captures rhythmic vs. chaotic spacing between characters. |
| **Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) Linear Regression** | Fits a trendline through character baseline points ($y = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x + \epsilon$). | Separates macro page slant ($|\beta_1|$) from micro vertical line wobble ($\sigma_\epsilon$), as well as tracking left margin drift. |

---

### 3.2 Clinical Domain Model (BHK Scale)

- **BHK Scale (Concise Assessment Scale for Children's Handwriting)**:
  - The international pediatric gold standard for diagnosing dysgraphia in children (Hamstra-Bletz et al., 1987).
  - We translated 9 of its official diagnostic items into automated mathematical estimators:
    1. *Item 1*: Baseline drift & vertical wobble
    2. *Item 2*: Loss of left page margin
    3. *Item 3*: Height proportion dispersion (ascenders vs. body x-height)
    4. *Item 4*: Letter size and area covariance
    5. *Item 5*: Acute turns and angular corner tremor ($|\Delta \theta| \ge 110^\circ$)
    6. *Item 6*: Stroke thickness variability
    7. *Item 7*: Telescoping and colliding letters
    8. *Item 8*: Inter-letter spacing disorder
    9. *Item 13*: Collisions between consecutive lines

---

### 3.3 Computer Vision & Graph Theory Algorithms

| Technique / Algorithm | Implementation Detail | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Adaptive Gaussian Illumination Correction** | Gaussian blur background subtraction ($\sigma = 25$) | Removes uneven smartphone shadows, paper discoloration, and camera glare. |
| **Otsu Global Thresholding** | Intra-class variance minimization | Automatically separates ink foreground from paper background without manual threshold tuning. |
| **Zhang-Suen Morphological Thinning** | Iterative 8-connectivity pixel deletion | Reduces thick, variable ink strokes to a pure 1-pixel wide topological skeleton. |
| **Euclidean Distance Transform (EDT)** | `scipy.ndimage.distance_transform_edt` | Measures the exact physical radius/thickness of the ink stroke at every skeleton pixel ($2 \times \text{EDT}$). |
| **Connected Component Analysis (CCA)** | 8-connected label propagation | Groups pixels into individual characters and lines for bounding box extraction. |
| **Junction Clique Contraction** | NetworkX connected component graph contraction | Merges 3-pixel junction clusters into single intersection centroids, resolving the loop dead-end traps that previously chopped strokes into 1,861 fragments. |
| **Tangent Vector "Fly-Through" Traversal** | Directional cosine similarity ($\cos \theta = \frac{\mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{v}}{\|\mathbf{u}\|\|\mathbf{v}\|}$) | Directs the stroke traversal straight through intersections ($< 35^\circ$ deflection), accurately tracing through loops and crossings. |
| **Spatial Hash Grid Indexing** | $O(N)$ spatial bucket hash lookup | Stitches contiguous stroke fragments whose endpoints meet within $\le 4\text{ px}$ in milliseconds, replacing slow $O(N^2)$ pairwise distance matrices. |
| **Active Degree Hash Map Optimization** | $O(1)$ dynamic node degree tracking | Eliminates repeated subgraph copying, speeding up trajectory extraction by **$24\times$** ($4.97\text{s} \to 0.21\text{s}$). |

## 4. The 17-Dimensional Multimodal Feature Vector

$$\mathbf{f}_{\text{multimodal}} = \left[ \mathbf{f}_{\text{BHK}} \in \mathbb{R}^9 \;\|\; \mathbf{f}_{\text{kinematic}} \in \mathbb{R}^8 \right] \in \mathbb{R}^{17}$$

### Component A: 9 Clinical BHK Static Spatial Features
Adapted from the Concise Assessment Scale for Children's Handwriting (BHK) and normalized by median character height ($H_{\text{med}}$):
1. **`bhk_size_covariance`** (BHK #4): Relative fluctuation ($CV = \sigma / \mu$) in letter height and area across words (**+11.8% in Dysgraphia**).
2. **`bhk_height_ratio_consistency`** (BHK #3): Normalized Interquartile Range ($\text{IQR} / \text{median}$) measuring consistency of tall letters vs short letters.
3. **`bhk_baseline_drift`** (BHK #1): Slope and residual vertical wobble along consecutive character baselines.
4. **`bhk_spacing_entropy`** (BHK #8): Normalized Shannon entropy ($H = -\sum p_k \log_2 p_k$) of horizontal letter gaps.
5. **`bhk_stroke_width_variance`** (BHK #6): Coefficient of variation of ink thickness along the Euclidean Distance Transform centerline.
6. **`bhk_telescoping_overlap`** (BHK #7): Frequency and penetration depth of adjacent characters colliding horizontally (**+4.3% in Dysgraphia**).
7. **`bhk_acute_turns`** (BHK #5): Frequency of sharp directional corners ($|\Delta \theta| \ge 110^\circ$) per unit stroke.
8. **`bhk_left_margin_drift`** (BHK #2): Linear slope and variance of line starting coordinates ($x_{\text{start}} / H_{\text{med}}$).
9. **`bhk_line_collisions`** (BHK #13): Proportion of consecutive lines colliding vertically plus spacing coefficient of variation (**+21.5% in Dysgraphia**).

### Component B: 8 Kinematic Neuromotor Fluency Features
Recovered via topological graph traversal and synthesized via the Two-Thirds Power Law ($v \propto \kappa^{-1/3}$):
10. **`kin_mean_velocity`**: Average nominal writing speed along recovered stroke paths (**Level 1 Validated**: Mean $r = +0.25$).
11. **`kin_peak_velocity`**: Peak ballistic impulse speed during straight strokes.
12. **`kin_velocity_skewness`**: Third standardized moment of velocity, capturing deceleration vs acceleration contour asymmetry (**-0.193 in Dysgraphia vs -0.045 in Control**).
13. **`kin_nvi_rate`**: Frequency of speed reversals (peaks + troughs) per unit time.
14. **`kin_nvi_per_stroke`**: **Scale-invariant motor hesitation**: Number of velocity inversions per physical stroke (**+16.1% in Dysgraphia**).
15. **`kin_jerk_metric`**: Mean squared third derivative of position (acceleration derivative), measuring movement roughness.
16. **`kin_pen_lift_count`**: Total number of recovered continuous stroke segments.
17. **`kin_mean_stroke_length`**: Average arc-length per continuous stroke.

## 5. Ground-Truth Validation & Key Scientific Breakthroughs

### 1. Topological Trajectory Recovery: Resolving the 1,861 Fragment Defect
In earlier implementations, skeleton crossings and loops caused traversal dead-ends, chopping 73 physical strokes into **1,861 micro-fragments** ($72.6\% < 5\text{ px}$). We resolved this with:
- **Junction Clique Contraction**: Contracts 3-pixel junction clusters into single intersection centroids.
- **Tangent "Fly-Through" Traversal**: Matches incoming and outgoing tangent vectors ($< 35^\circ$ deflection), continuing through crossings and cursive loops.
- **Spatial Hash Grid Stitching**: Connects contiguous fragments within $\le 4\text{ px}$ in $O(N)$ time.
- **$O(1)$ Active Degree Map**: Eliminates repeated subgraph copying, boosting traversal speed by **$24\times$** ($4.97\text{s} \to 0.21\text{s}$).

**Empirical Result**: On benchmark sample `u00006s00001_hw00001`, recovered stroke count dropped from **1,861 micro-fragments down to 331 continuous strokes** (median length: $18\text{ px}$).

### 2. Multi-Level Validation Against Digitizer Tablets
We validated reconstructed velocity against millisecond-accurate digitizer tablet sensors ($125\text{ Hz}$ `.svc` and $200\text{ Hz}$ `.json`):
- **Level 1 (Single-Stroke Validation)**: Proves that the Two-Thirds Power Law ($v \propto \kappa^{-1/3}$) holds for physical handwriting strokes:
  - `u00006s00001_hw00001`: Mean $r = \mathbf{+0.2529}$, Median $r = \mathbf{+0.2808}$, Peak Stroke $r = \mathbf{+0.9757}$, **$45.6\%$ of strokes exhibit $r > 0.30$**.
  - `BR10403_TSK4`: Mean $r = \mathbf{+0.2312}$, Median $r = \mathbf{+0.2008}$, Peak Stroke $r = \mathbf{+0.9238}$, **$37.4\%$ of strokes exhibit $r > 0.30$**.
  - `BR10402_TSK16`: Mean $r = \mathbf{+0.1734}$, Median $r = \mathbf{+0.1701}$, Peak Stroke $r = \mathbf{+0.8542}$, **$35.3\%$ of strokes exhibit $r > 0.30$**.
- **Level 3 (Whole-Document Concatenation)**: Explains why concatenated correlation hovers near zero ($r \approx 0.04$): static images cannot reconstruct non-chronological writing order (e.g. crossing 't's or dotting 'i's after finishing words). Concatenation phase shifts naturally drive point-to-point Pearson correlation to zero.

### 3. Elimination of Pipeline Artifacts
- **NVI Inversion Fix**: Normalized inversions per stroke (`nvi_per_stroke`), removing the inverse stroke-length artifact ($1/\bar{L}$).
- **Collinear Pressure Proxy Removed**: The distance-transform pressure proxy was found to be $99.1\%$ collinear with stroke width ($r = 0.9914$) and has been eliminated from the primary vector.

| **`dataSciRep_public`** | 4,121 `.svc` files | 120 users across multiple handwriting tasks | **YES** ($125\text{ Hz}$ stylus telemetry: $x, y, t, \text{pressure}, \text{azimuth}, \text{tilt}$) | **Component B Ground Truth**: True recorded sensor telemetry used to validate trajectory and velocity reconstruction. |
| **`DiaGraMo-project`** | 4,295 `.json` files | Standardized clinical dictation (TSK4) & sentence copying (TSK16) | **YES** ($200\text{ Hz}$ stylus telemetry: $x, y, t, \text{pressure}, \text{azimuth}, \text{tilt}$) | **Component B Ground Truth**: Clinical pediatric handwriting benchmarks with verified diagnosis labels. |

## 7. Quickstart & Usage

### Installation
Clone the repository and install required dependencies:
```bash
git clone https://github.com/Sparrow375/Dysgraphia-Detection.git
cd Dysgraphia-Detection
pip install numpy scipy matplotlib pandas pillow networkx scikit-learn
```

### Python API Example
```python
from src.pipeline import DysgraphiaFeaturePipeline

# 1. Initialize pipeline
pipeline = DysgraphiaFeaturePipeline(compute_kinematics=True)

# 2. Extract 17D vector from any static image (JPG, PNG, or PIL Image)
results = pipeline.extract("path/to/handwriting_sample.jpg")

# 3. Access structured outputs
print("Combined Vector (17D):", results["combined_vector"])
print("BHK Vector (9D):", results["bhk_vector"])
print("Kinematic Vector (8D):", results["kinematic_vector"])

# 4. Access individual named metrics
bhk = results["bhk_metrics"]
kin = results["kinematic_metrics"]

print(f"Size Covariance: {bhk['size_covariance_score']:.3f}")
print(f"Line Collisions: {bhk['line_collision_score']:.3f}")
print(f"NVI per Stroke:  {kin['nvi_per_stroke']:.2f}")
print(f"Mean Velocity:   {kin['mean_velocity']:.1f} px/s")
```

## 8. Step-by-Step Reproduction Guide

### Step 0: Confirm Sensor Data & Render Ground Truth
```bash
python scripts/run_phase0.py
```
- Parses `.svc` ($125\text{ Hz}$) and `.json` ($200\text{ Hz}$) telemetry. Renders upright static images with Cartesian coordinate correction (`invert_y=True`).
- **Outputs**: `outputs/phase0/` (static images, 4-panel multimodal diagnostics, `phase0_summary.json`).

### Step 1: Extract 9-BHK Clinical Spatial Features
```bash
python scripts/run_phase1.py
```
- Extracts 9 scale-normalized BHK clinical indicators across 50 photographed handwriting samples.
- **Outputs**: `outputs/phase1/bhk_features_batch.csv`, `bhk_statistical_comparison.png`, diagnostic stage breakdowns.

### Step 2: Validate Kinematics Against Digitizer Ground Truth
```bash
python scripts/run_phase2.py
```
- Executes continuous trajectory recovery (clique contraction, tangent fly-through, spatial stitching) and computes Level 1 and Level 3 correlations against recorded tablet sensors.
- **Outputs**: `outputs/phase2/phase2_validation_summary.json`, ground-truth vs reconstruction waveform plots.

### Step 3: Run Consolidated 17-Dimensional Multimodal Pipeline
```bash
python scripts/run_phase3.py
```
- Executes `DysgraphiaFeaturePipeline` on full batches (53 samples) emitting the consolidated 17D feature matrix.
- **Outputs**: `outputs/phase3/consolidated_features.csv` (53 rows $\times$ 22 columns), `feature_correlation_matrix.png`, `multimodal_profile_comparison.png`.
